text:
ivy: Hey team 94 first-week M2 question. I'm trying to combine Nix-based dev shells with asdf for node/python. Homebrew is at /opt/homebrew. I'm seeing python builds fail with missing ssl/zlib, and 1Password's SSH agent isn't picked up when I launch apps from the Dock. What's a small, reliable checklist to get a clean bootstrap?

alex: Welcome! :wave: Short checklist that helped me when mixing Nix + asdf on mac: 1) Make sure asdf shims are early on PATH (in your login shell file). 2) For building python/rust/node, expose Homebrew libs to the build environment (Nix doesn't provide /opt/homebrew by default). Example env bits (bash/zsh):
```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.asdf/shims:$HOME/.asdf/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH"
export LDFLAGS="-L/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@3/lib -L/opt/homebrew/opt/zlib/lib"
export CPPFLAGS="-I/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@3/include -I/opt/homebrew/opt/zlib/include"
export PKG_CONFIG_PATH="/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@3/lib/pkgconfig:/opt/homebrew/opt/zlib/lib/pkgconfig"
```
Then `asdf reshim` and retry `asdf install python 3.11.x`.

soren: For 1Password agent on mac, there's a recent change where the CLI daemon exposes a different socket depending on how you authenticated. Find the socket with:
```bash
lsof -U | rg 1password || gpgconf --list-dirs agent-ssh-socket
```
If you see something like `/Users/ivy/.1password/agent.sock` export it in your login file: `export SSH_AUTH_SOCK=/Users/ivy/.1password/agent.sock`. Note: apps launched from the Dock inherit launchctl env, not your shell. If you want GUI apps to see the socket, either: a) launch VSCode from terminal (`code .`), or b) use `launchctl setenv SSH_AUTH_SOCK $SSH_AUTH_SOCK` after exporting so Finder apps pick it up.

maya: Extra Nix tip: if you're using direnv + nix-direnv, ensure `direnv allow` ran and your shell actually sources direnv hook. For fish add `direnv hook fish | source` in config.fish. Also, Nix builds isolate /usr/include, so pointing LDFLAGS/PKG_CONFIG_PATH at brew is mandatory for asdf plugins that compile openssl-dependent libs.

ivy: I had direnv enabled but forgot to add the nix hook in fish, so my asdf env didn't see LDFLAGS. Added the exports to ~/.config/fish/config.fish (converted to `set -x` form) and re-ran asdf. Build still errored once with "ssl not found" but logs showed pkg-config couldn't find openssl.

alex: run `pkg-config --exists openssl && pkg-config --libs openssl` to debug; if it prints nothing, PKG_CONFIG_PATH is wrong. On mac arm sometimes you need to install `pkg-config` via brew too: `brew install pkg-config openssl@3`.

soren: small trick for debugging agent problems in GUI apps: from your graphical app terminal (Terminal.app or iTerm opened from Finder), run `echo $SSH_AUTH_SOCK` and `ssh-add -l`. If empty, either export via launchctl or relaunch the GUI app from a terminal. Also check 1Password > Developer > Agent socket path.

ops-bot: Reminder: new hires should tick off the dev-tooling checklist on the onboarding doc (https://intranet.redwood/dev-onboard). Step: "dev-shells & ssh" is often overlooked.

ivy: Follow-up: after exporting PKG_CONFIG_PATH and installing pkg-config, `pkg-config --libs openssl` returned a path. `asdf install python 3.11.4` succeeded after `exec $SHELL`. For the agent, `launchctl setenv SSH_AUTH_SOCK $SSH_AUTH_SOCK` made VSCode-from-dock see my key.

maya: Nice! One more: please open a tiny PR to the dotfiles repo updating macos/arm/README.md with the nix + asdf snippet and the launchctl tip. We have a template under docs/templates/PR_NOTE.md.

dotfiles-bot: Please include a brief changelog entry and reference the onboarding checklist step.

ivy: Will do 94 thanks everyone, saved me a bunch of trial-and-error. Ping me if you want me to include the fish snippet in the PR as well.
